- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day mean, forecast should be pulled toward mean; if below, pull upward — especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% immediately.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model tends to ignore sentiment; if sentiment >0.67 and price < previous 5-day low, apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- Model underestimates price drops after strong positive sentiment; if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior and price drops sharply, add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
